correctness.rationale: For fixed positive information weights the nonnegative invasion matrix is positively diagonally similar to an affine symmetric matrix, so the largest eigenvalue is convex by Rayleigh–Ritz. In the biregular subclass a strictly positive quotient eigenvector lifts to the full graph, proving equation (1); the exact second derivative and characteristic-derivative elimination prove the unique interior minimum and parameter criterion. The K4, six-person matching, cross-incidence graph satisfies n1<n2, tau<1, positive probabilities and has critical roots (7±sqrt7)/48. Symbolic identities, the ten-by-ten eigenvalue example, and parameter checks were executed from the standalone checker. Boundary equality is deliberately not classified nonlinearly.

value.rationale: The source reports network-dependent changes in the epidemic threshold but not a structural condition. The convexity theorem forbids intermediate invasion when both commuting endpoints are safe, while the exact equitable-class condition and sharp ten-person construction identify when intermediate commuting protects against invasion despite two unsafe extremes. This is a model-specific, nontrivial network ecology/epidemiology decision boundary, not simply a numerical simulation, and its interpretation is confined to local linear invasion.
